A very small amount of material — on the order of 100 grams to less than 2 kilograms, typically calcium carbonate (a common mineral found in limestone and used in products such as toothpaste) — would be released into a small mixed volume roughly 1 km long and 100 meters in diameter. The gondola would then fly back through that plume to measure aerosol microphysics, chemistry, and light scattering. In March 2024 Harvard announced that Keutsch was no longer pursuing SCoPEx; the platform is expected to be repurposed for stratospheric research unrelated to solar geoengineering.
